subject: Operational reliability tolerance & fixed monthly remedy bucket
messages:
From: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay.mehta@polarishealthtech.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>; ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amelia Torres <amelia.torres@polarishealthtech.com>; procurement@polarishealthtech.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Polaris request: swap percentage credits for fixed monthly remedy bucket

Tessa / Ben —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our procurement team dug into the draft SLA and we have a single structural ask: instead of the classic percentage-of-month credits (e.g., X% of monthly fees), Polaris would prefer a fixed "monthly remedy bucket" capped at a dollar figure for planned and unplanned remedies.

High-level rationale: predictable financial exposure is important for our board and procurement; the percentage model produces ambiguity in months with heavy usage spikes. We still want an availability guarantee, but want the remedy to be a capped, standalone monthly credit (example ask: $15,000/month) rather than proportional credits.

Other asks we want considered:
- Availability target: keep 99.95% for core hosted endpoints, but allow a combined latency SLO (95th pct < 220ms) with clear measurement windows.
- Maintenance carve-outs: standard maintenance windows ok, but we need 72-hour advance notice for any maintenance that impacts regional routing.
- Remedy triggers: clarify whether a brief regional blip (e.g., 10 minutes) would trigger a proportional percentage or fall under aggregated monthly accounting.

Can you confirm whether Redwood would agree to a capped monthly remedy bucket and if so what the dollar cap would look like for our current commitment level?

Appreciate a quick note — we need to consolidate procurement input by next Wednesday (25th).

Thanks,
Sanjay
VP Procurement, Polaris Healthtech
---
Attachments: Polaris_SOW_Draft_v3.pdf
From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay.mehta@polarishealthtech.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Polaris request: swap percentage credits for fixed monthly remedy bucket

Sanjay —

Thanks for the clear ask and the rationale. We can absolutely discuss a fixed monthly remedy bucket; it’s a common procurement preference. A few quick notes from our side:

- We typically pair an availability floor (e.g., 99.95%) with a proportional credit ladder to keep incentives aligned. Replacing that with a fixed bucket is workable, but we’ll want to ensure the cap scales with committed spend to avoid misalignment on very large contracts.

- For measurement and triggers, we rely on monthly aggregation windows and region-aware telemetry; short regional blips become material when they impact customer traffic for >1% of the month. We can produce a sample calculation so you can see how an event maps to credit consumption.

- Maintenance notices (72-hour minimum) — we can add a contractual commitment there for scheduled maintenance that impacts routing.

Ben and Laura — looping you in to propose a calibrated cap and a short redline on the remedy language. Sanjay — can we schedule a 30-min call tomorrow at 10am PT to walk through a proposed structure? If that doesn't work, propose another slot.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

---

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>; Sanjay Mehta <sanjay.mehta@polarishealthtech.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Polaris request: swap percentage credits for fixed monthly remedy bucket

Sanjay / Tessa / Laura —

Following our internal review, here's a pragmatic starting point that should be simple to present internally at Polaris and preserve our mutual risk alignment:

Proposal (starter):
- Keep Availability: 99.95% monthly for production endpoints (as measured by Redwood's telemetry with region-specific breakdown).
- Replace the percentage-of-revenue credit ladder with a fixed monthly remedy bucket set relative to committed spend tiers. For Polaris' current projected committed monthly consumption (~$120k MRR equivalent), propose a fixed bucket of $12,000/month. This is roughly 10% of committed monthly spend (keeps downside aligned).
- Remedy exhausts in order of events; once bucket is consumed the remedy for additional breaches becomes credit-only at a capped monthly limit (i.e., no additional cash payouts).
- Latency: agree to a 95th percentile <220ms target on core routes; allow for a small penalty threshold that draws down the remedy bucket (we can define a simple per-incident credit factor in the attached SLA_credits_table.xlsx).
- Maintenance: 72-hour notice for impactful maintenance; standard maintenance windows excluded from availability calculations.

Next steps: Laura, can you draft a short redline for the SLA section replacing percentage credits with a fixed-bucket construct and a simple table tying committed spend tiers to bucket amounts? Sanjay — if $12k/month is not acceptable, tell us a target number and we'll iterate.

Happy to jump on a call tomorrow at 10am PT if that works.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: SLA_credits_table.xlsx
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay.mehta@polarishealthtech.com>; ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>; tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Draft redline: fixed monthly remedy bucket (polaris)

Sanjay / Ben / Tessa —

I've attached a redline and summarized the key contractual changes below. This is written to be procurement-friendly while protecting Redwood from disproportional exposure.

Summary of redline highlights:
1) Fixed Monthly Remedy Bucket: replace percentage-based credits with a fixed monthly credit bucket tied to committed spend tiers. For reference, table maps: <$50k => $4k/mo; $50k-$150k => $12k/mo; >$150k => $25k/mo. (Polaris falls in the second tier based on current forecast.)

2) Aggregation and Exhaustion: credits are applied against qualifying Availability breaches in the month. If the bucket is exhausted, further breaches in the same month do not create additional credits beyond an agreed escalation path (we suggest a quarterly review to recalibrate caps).

3) Definition of Availability & Measurement: keep 99.95% as the monthly target. Include region-split reporting and an explicit measurement method (Redwood telemetry, 1-minute sampling, 00:00–23:59 UTC aggregation).

4) Latency Remedies: latency measured at 95th percentile across customer traffic; breaches map to a multiplier that draws down the monthly bucket. We avoid micro-penalties per short blip to prevent tokenization of noise.

5) Maintenance: 72-hour notice for maintenance that may affect routing; scheduled maintenance windows pre-announced and excluded.

6) Audit & Transparency: provide monthly availability and latency report and shared dashboard access; optional third-party audit clause for annual review.

Sanjay — please confirm whether Polaris can accept the fixed-dollar cap at $12k/month for the current commitment. If Polaris asks for $15k, we will need to move Polaris up a committed tier or add a one-time purchase credit to bridge the gap for the first 90 days.

If this is acceptable in principle, I can produce a short contract amendment and we can route for signature. If not, happy to jump on the call to negotiate specific numbers.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: Polaris_SOW_Draft_v3.pdf (referenced)
From: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay.mehta@polarishealthtech.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>; ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>; tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 11:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Draft redline: fixed monthly remedy bucket (polaris)

Laura / Ben / Tessa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear table. Polaris can accept the $12k/month fixed bucket if Redwood will include the following limited concessions:

1) A provisioning clause that allows Polaris to request a one-time "initial buffer" of $3k for the first month only (to smooth onboarding risk) — effectively making the first month $15k total available credits.
2) A commitment to a quarterly review clause with automatic upward recalibration of the bucket if committed monthly spend increases >15%.
3) A clear example calculation in the SOW appendix that maps a sample partial regional outage (30m affecting 40% of traffic in a region) to the credit deduction from the bucket so our finance team can reconcile.

If Redwood signs up to those three items, procurement can greenlight execution and we can move to signature. We also want the 72-hour maintenance notice expressly added in the amendment.

Let me know and we’ll loop legal to finalize.

Best,
Sanjay
VP Procurement, Polaris Healthtech
